version.changelog:
### Changelog for self-improving-agent v4.0.3

## Added
- Cause-aware maintenance for saved knowledge, including one-off and unpromoted learnings.
- Four decay types determine how to revalidate: reality, decision, dependency, and relevance.
- Qualitative review rates—fast, medium, slow, and durable—determine when to check. Relevant changes override cadence.
- Lightweight maintenance metadata records each claim’s scope, authority, review triggers, and actual dated evidence.

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed local learning/memory workflow with optional hooks; it is not malicious, but users should understand it persists notes and can update workspace guidance files.

dimensions.detail: The optional hook reads ended session transcripts for error patterns and writes short redacted excerpts only when a .learnings directory exists. Cross-session transcript access and messaging are documented as trusted-environment, explicit-user-intent actions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is via the OpenClaw installer, ClawHub CLI, or manual git clone/copy. The hook is explicitly optional and uninstall instructions are scoped to the skill, hook, and learning directories.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger language is broad and encourages automatic logging of corrections, feature requests, knowledge gaps, and errors, but it also instructs agents not to log secrets, raw transcripts, or full files, and to validate claims before reuse or promotion.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent .learnings files and possible promotion into SOUL.md, TOOLS.md, or AGENTS.md are central to the skill and clearly disclosed. This is meaningful persistent agent-memory behavior, so users should review what gets stored or promoted.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently describe capture, review, maintenance, and optional promotion of learnings/errors for OpenClaw. The broader pieces, including setup, optional hook, cross-session sharing guidance, and skill extraction, are disclosed and tied to the self-improvement purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want OpenClaw to keep local persistent learning notes and, when appropriate, update workspace guidance files. Keep .learnings out of version control unless you intentionally want to share it, review promoted SOUL.md/TOOLS.md/AGENTS.md changes, and enable the hook only if you accept session-end transcript scanning for redacted error excerpts.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The scanner correctly noticed install, hook, promotion, communication, and extraction workflows, but these are documented in the skill and fit the stated self-improvement purpose rather than being hidden tool poisoning.
[RA1] expected: The cited self-modification text actually requires explicit scoped approval before creating or modifying skill assets, so it reduces rather than creates uncontrolled self-modification risk.
[P3] expected: sessions_send is cross-session OpenClaw messaging, not an external exfiltration command; the artifact says to use it only when explicitly wanted and to send sanitized summaries.
[TM1] expected: The rm -r commands appear in uninstall instructions for removing the skill, hook, or captured learnings and are preceded by warnings to review or archive user data.
[LP3] expected: Filesystem writes, shell setup commands, and optional hook behavior are part of the documented workflow, though the package does not provide a separate machine-readable permission boundary.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad logging triggers are purpose-aligned for a memory skill, but users should be aware they can persist ordinary conversation-derived corrections or feature requests.
[RA2] expected: Persistent .learnings files and hook-created pending error entries are expected for this skill, locally scoped, and gated by setup or the presence of the .learnings directory.
[AS3] unexpected: The cited other-skill path is a historical example in documentation, not an instruction to enumerate or read installed peer skills.
[EA2] expected: The uninstall guide explicitly says promoted content is not automatically removed and must be manually reviewed, so it does not direct autonomous deletion of workspace guidance.
[AIG-SARIF] expected: The supplied A.I.G SARIF run reported no results; local inspection likewise did not find embedded malicious code, remote payload execution, credential theft, or destructive automatic behavior.
